title: API Management Overview
description: Get an introduction to Azure API Management and how it helps you publish, govern, and monetize APIs.

data.text: Azure API Management (APIM) is a turnkey solution for publishing APIs to external and internal consumers. It acts as a gateway in front of your APIs, adding security, throttling, caching, and transformation without changing the backend.
APIM has three components: the gateway (proxy), the management plane (Azure Portal or ARM), and the developer portal (a website where consumers discover and test APIs).

data.title: APIM Benefits
items: Publish APIs with a unified front door
Secure APIs with keys, OAuth, and JWT validation
Throttle and quota requests per user or subscription
Transform requests and responses with policies
Monetize APIs with products and subscriptions

data.title: Create an APIM Instance with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision an APIM Developer tier instance.
data.code: az apim create   --name myApim   --resource-group myRG   --location eastus   --publisher-email admin@example.com   --publisher-name "My Organization"   --sku-name Developer

data.caption: APIM sits between consumers and your backend APIs.
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    Consumer["API Consumer"] -->|"HTTPS"| APIM["API Management"]
    APIM -->|"Policies, auth, throttle"| Backend["Backend API"]
    Backend -->|"Response"| APIM
    APIM -->|"Response"| Consumer

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: APIM is a gateway that manages, secures, and monetizes APIs.
It sits in front of your backends, so consumers never touch them directly.
Policies are the core extensibility mechanism in APIM.
data.takeaway: Use APIM whenever you need to share APIs with partners or internal teams securely.
